question.text: A student measuring the diameter of a pencil of circular cross-section with the help of a vernier scale records the following four readings <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>55</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>34</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>65</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. The average of these four reading is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5375</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> and the standard deviation of the data is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>07395</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. The average diameter of the pencil should therefore be recorded as :

solution.text:
Significant rule says that reading should has same significant figure as that of reading given.

5.5375→ rounded to →5.54.

0.07395→ rounded to→0.07

therefore, 5.54±0.07 mm
